 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by claim petitioners 2 to 4 in O.P.(MV) No.369/2007 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thrissur, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 02/04/2019.
The respondents herein are respondents 1 and 2 respectively in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioners, on 24/01/2006 at 09:00 p.m., while the original claim petitioner was riding his bicycle through the Thrissur-Palakkad NH-47 and when he reached the place by name Chemboothra, motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-12/4636 ridden by the first respondent in a rash and 2025:KER:74442 MACA NO. 987 OF 2020 negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries to which he succumbed on 07/09/2008.
A sum of 9,28,500/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner-cum-rider of the offending vehicle though appeared and filed vakalath, did not file any written statement.

4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle, but denied negligence on the part of the first respondent/owner-cum-rider.
The age, income etc., of the original claim petitioner were disputed.
It was contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
It was also contended that the case cannot be treated as a death case since there was no postmortem certificate and as the death had occurred two and half years after the accident.

5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to 2025:KER:74442 MACA NO. 987 OF 2020 A11 and Ext.X1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners and Ext.B1 was marked on the side of the second respondent/insurer.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent/owner-cum-rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,91,590/- together with interest @ 8%
per annum from the date of the petition till realization along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioners have come up in appeal.

Jalaja vs A.C.George on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47615505/
2 7.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioners - 2025:KER:74442 MACA NO. 987 OF 2020 Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners that 5,000/- fixed by the Tribunal as the notional income of the original claim petitioner is low going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, 9.1.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the income of a coolie in the year 2006 is liable to be fixed at 5,500/-.
Hence, I find that the notional income of the original claim petitioner can also be fixed as 5,500/- per month.
Compensation for permanent disability 10.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners that the injuries sustained by the original claim petitioner were quite grievous which resulted in his death.

However, the Tribunal treated the case as an injury case and awarded compensation accordingly, which is an error committed by the Tribunal which needs to be interfered with and the matter 2025:KER:74442 MACA NO. 987 OF 2020 treated as a death case.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the second respondent/insurer that no postmortem was conducted and there are no materials on record to show that the death was caused due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
That being the position, the Tribunal was right in treating the case as an injury case and awarding compensation accordingly.
10.1. Admittedly, no postmortem was conducted.
The accident took place on 24/01/2006 and the original claim petitioner died on 07/09/2008.
Ext.A7 discharge summary issued by Thrissur Heart Hospital Ltd. shows that he was admitted on 25/01/2006 at 12:27 a.m. and discharged on 17/02/2006.

The final diagnosis reads thus:
"Acute SDH (R) side with contusion (R) temperoparietal region/(L) frontral ICH/right fronto parietal craniotomy & evacuation of acute SDH under G.A."
As per Ext.A7, when he was discharged on 17/02/2006, he was advised review after a week.

Thereafter, another discharge summary issued by Kovoor Institute of Neuro Science (KINS),
2025:KER:74442 MACA NO. 987 OF 2020 Sakthan Thampuran Nagar, Thrissur, shows that he was admitted in the hospital on 04/03/02006 and was discharged on 11/03/2006.

In page no.1 of the said document, the relevant portion reads thus:
"History and Physical findings:
Patient still bed ridden unable to walk without support (not legible) feeds.
Not talking or responding well ..............."

Jalaja vs A.C.George on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47615505/
3

The relevant portion in page no.2 reads thus:
Hospital stay, treatment, discussion:
Patient improved on physically, able to walk better, (not legible) catheter removed."
(Emphasis supplied)
Therefore, the second discharge certificate shows that the condition of the claim petitioner had improved and he was also in a position to walk.
Apart from Ext.A7, there is no other medical record(s) to show the physical condition or state of the original claim petitioner.
The fourth claim petitioner, namely, the daughter of the origin claim petitioner, offered herself as a witness and was examined before the Tribunal as PW1.

PW1 has a case that her 2025:KER:74442 MACA NO.
987 OF 2020 father was completely bed ridden and depending on others after the accident.
As noticed earlier, apart from Ext.A7, there are no other medical records to show the medical condition of the original claim petitioner.
There is also no disability certificate in this case.
Therefore, this Court is seriously handicapped in arriving at the percentage of functional disability caused to the original claim petitioner.
However, taking into account the testimony of PW1 read along with Ext.A7, I find that a consolidated amount can be awarded as disability compensation.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, 6,00,000/- seems to be a reasonable amount, which can be granted under this head.
Loss of earnings 11.
The Tribunal treating the case as an injury case awarded loss of earnings for a period of 32 months.
The accident took place on 24/01/2006 and the original claim petitioner died on 07/09/2008, that is, after a period of 2  years.
Hence, 32 months was taken as the period for which he had lost his earnings.

As a lumpsum amount 2025:KER:74442 MACA NO. 987 OF 2020 has already been granted towards permanent disability treating the case as an injury case, I find that the amount awarded under this head requires modification.
As noticed earlier, there are no other medical records to show the condition of the original claim petitioner.
In these circumstances, this Court can only enter into a guess work and decide upon the period for which he can be awarded loss of earnings.
The accident took place on 24/01/2006.
The second discharge certificate in Ext.A7 shows that he was admitted on 04/03/2006 and he was discharged on 11/03/2006.
As compensation has already been awarded for disability, I find that loss of earnings for a period of 4 months can be granted, which comes to 22,000/- (5,500 x 4 months).

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 4,62,000/- (total compensation = 8,53,590/- that is, 3,91,590/-
granted by the Tribunal plus 4,62,000/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 118 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The second respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
